question_text: Which of the following correctly describes toxicokinetics?

options.B: Cannot be used for risk assessment
options.C: Toxicokinetics is the quantitative study of ADME through measurement of concentrations in biological matrices vs time

explanation: Toxicokinetics is the quantitative study of ADME through measurement of concentrations in biological matrices vs time. Derived from pharmacokinetics studies with drugs

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes toxicokinetics?

options.C: Cmax and AUC are the two most common dose metrics in toxicokinetic studies
options.D: Cannot be used for risk assessment

explanation: Cmax and AUC are the two most common dose metrics in toxicokinetic studies. Cmax is peak concentration; AUC is area under concentration-time curve

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes toxicokinetics?

options.A: Cannot be used for risk assessment
options.C: Does not account for metabolism
options.D: The trapezoidal method calculates AUC by summing areas of trapezoids from the concentration-time curve

explanation: The trapezoidal method calculates AUC by summing areas of trapezoids from the concentration-time curve. AUC0-inf adds Clast/Kel for terminal area

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes toxicokinetics?

options.C: Only applies to drugs
options.D: Cannot be used for risk assessment

explanation: Mean residence time (MRT) = AUMC/AUC. AUMC is area under first moment curve (concentration x time)

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes toxicokinetics?

options.A: Cannot be used for risk assessment
options.C: Does not account for metabolism
options.D: At least 2 early and 3 terminal elimination phase time points needed for TK studies

explanation: At least 2 early and 3 terminal elimination phase time points needed for TK studies. Samples should show concentration changes by factor of 2 or order of magnitude

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes toxicokinetics?

options.C: Cannot be used for risk assessment
options.D: No more than 10% of blood volume should be drawn during AUC sampling interval

explanation: No more than 10% of blood volume should be drawn during AUC sampling interval. Prevents compromising physiological status

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes toxicokinetics?

options.A: One-compartment model assumes body as single homogeneous compartment with instantaneous distribution
options.B: Cannot be used for risk assessment
options.C: Always linear across all doses

explanation: One-compartment model assumes body as single homogeneous compartment with instantaneous distribution. Appropriate for rapidly distributing compounds

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes toxicokinetics?

options.B: Cannot be used for risk assessment
options.C: PBTK models incorporate actual anatomical and physiological parameters (tissue volumes, blood flows, partition coefficients)

explanation: PBTK models incorporate actual anatomical and physiological parameters (tissue volumes, blood flows, partition coefficients). Allows mechanistic prediction of tissue concentrations

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes toxicokinetics?

options.A: Clearance is the volume of blood completely cleared of chemical per unit time
options.C: Cannot be used for risk assessment

explanation: Clearance is the volume of blood completely cleared of chemical per unit time. Hepatic clearance depends on intrinsic clearance, blood flow, and protein binding

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes toxicokinetics?

options.A: Cannot be used for risk assessment
options.C: Always linear across all doses
options.D: Elimination half-life: t1/2 = 0.693/ke for first-order elimination

explanation: Elimination half-life: t1/2 = 0.693/ke for first-order elimination. Half-life doubles when clearance decreases by half

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes toxicokinetics?

options.A: Bioavailability F = AUC_oral / (AUC_IV x dose_oral/dose_IV) x 100%
options.B: Cannot be used for risk assessment
options.C: Always linear across all doses

explanation: Bioavailability F = AUC_oral / (AUC_IV x dose_oral/dose_IV) x 100%. F < 100% indicates incomplete absorption or first-pass metabolism

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes toxicokinetics?

options.C: Cannot be used for risk assessment
options.D: Nonlinear kinetics occur when elimination processes become saturated at high doses

explanation: Nonlinear kinetics occur when elimination processes become saturated at high doses. AUC increases disproportionately; half-life may increase

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes air pollution?

options.B: No health effects at ambient levels
options.C: PM2.5 is more harmful than PM10 because smaller particles penetrate deeper into alveoli

explanation: PM2.5 is more harmful than PM10 because smaller particles penetrate deeper into alveoli. PM10 is largely deposited in upper airways

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes air pollution?

options.B: No health effects at ambient levels
options.C: Only affects respiratory system
options.D: Ground-level ozone is a secondary pollutant formed by photochemical reactions of NOx and VOCs

explanation: Ground-level ozone is a secondary pollutant formed by photochemical reactions of NOx and VOCs. Causes respiratory inflammation and decreased lung function

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes air pollution?

options.A: No health effects at ambient levels
options.B: EPA NAAQS set limits for criteria pollutants including PM2.5, PM10, O3, CO, SO2, NO2, and lead
options.C: Exclusively outdoor phenomenon

explanation: EPA NAAQS set limits for criteria pollutants including PM2.5, PM10, O3, CO, SO2, NO2, and lead. NAAQS are set to protect public health with adequate margin of safety

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes analytical tox?

options.C: Sample preparation not required
options.D: GC-MS is the gold standard for volatile and semi-volatile compound identification in forensic toxicology

explanation: GC-MS is the gold standard for volatile and semi-volatile compound identification in forensic toxicology. Provides chromatographic separation and mass spectral identification

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes analytical tox?

options.A: LC-MS/MS has replaced immunoassay for confirmatory drug testing due to higher specificity
options.C: Immunoassays provide definitive ID

explanation: LC-MS/MS has replaced immunoassay for confirmatory drug testing due to higher specificity. MRM provides excellent selectivity and sensitivity

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes analytical tox?

options.C: Immunoassays are used for initial screening but can produce false positives due to cross-reactivity

explanation: Immunoassays are used for initial screening but can produce false positives due to cross-reactivity. Confirmation by GC-MS or LC-MS/MS is required

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes clinical tox?

options.C: N-acetylcysteine (NAC) is the antidote for acetaminophen toxicity, replenishing glutathione

explanation: N-acetylcysteine (NAC) is the antidote for acetaminophen toxicity, replenishing glutathione. Most effective within 8-10 hours of ingestion

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes clinical tox?

options.B: Atropine blocks muscarinic effects in organophosphate poisoning but does not reverse nicotinic effects
options.C: Activated charcoal contraindicated always

explanation: Atropine blocks muscarinic effects in organophosphate poisoning but does not reverse nicotinic effects. Pralidoxime is needed for AChE reactivation

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes occupational tox?

options.C: PPE is only protection needed
options.D: TLV-TWA is the 8-hour time-weighted average; TLV-STEL is 15-minute; TLV-C is ceiling

explanation: TLV-TWA is the 8-hour time-weighted average; TLV-STEL is 15-minute; TLV-C is ceiling. TLVs are guidelines, not legally enforceable (unlike OSHA PELs)

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes occupational tox?

options.A: Biological Exposure Indices (BEIs) complement air monitoring by reflecting total exposure via all routes
options.C: TLV-TWA is enforceable law

explanation: Biological Exposure Indices (BEIs) complement air monitoring by reflecting total exposure via all routes. BEIs are guidelines for levels in biological specimens

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes regulatory tox?

options.A: TSCA regulates chemical substances in commerce through EPA pre-manufacture notification
options.C: FIFRA does not require efficacy data

explanation: TSCA regulates chemical substances in commerce through EPA pre-manufacture notification. EPA can require testing and restrict new chemicals

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes regulatory tox?

options.B: FIFRA requires EPA registration of all pesticides with mammalian toxicity, environmental fate, and efficacy data
options.C: Regulatory requirements identical worldwide

explanation: FIFRA requires EPA registration of all pesticides with mammalian toxicity, environmental fate, and efficacy data. Registration must be renewed periodically

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes study design?

options.A: Subchronic studies are 90-day rodent and 6-month non-rodent studies to identify target organs
options.C: Only one dose level needed

explanation: Subchronic studies are 90-day rodent and 6-month non-rodent studies to identify target organs. Used to establish dose ranges for chronic studies

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes study design?

options.C: Satellite groups always sacrificed at interim
options.D: Chronic rodent studies are typically 2 years (lifetime) to detect carcinogenic potential

explanation: Chronic rodent studies are typically 2 years (lifetime) to detect carcinogenic potential. Minimum 50 animals/sex/group for carcinogenicity studies

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes study design?

options.C: Satellite groups provide interim sacrifices or recovery assessments in toxicity studies

explanation: Satellite groups provide interim sacrifices or recovery assessments in toxicity studies. Recovery groups assess reversibility of treatment effects

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes study design?

options.B: Satellite groups always sacrificed at interim
options.C: Only one dose level needed
options.D: The maximum tolerated dose (MTD) is the highest dose that does not shorten survival by >10%

explanation: The maximum tolerated dose (MTD) is the highest dose that does not shorten survival by >10%. Used as high dose in carcinogenicity bioassays

question_text: All of the following are correct regarding carcinogenicity EXCEPT:

options.A: Tumor incidence not adjusted for mortality
options.C: Only one species required
options.D: The 2-year rodent bioassay is the gold standard for carcinogenicity assessment

explanation: The 2-year rodent bioassay is the gold standard for carcinogenicity assessment. Uses rats and mice at 3 dose levels plus controls

question_text: All of the following are correct regarding carcinogenicity EXCEPT:

options.B: The polyk adjustment accounts for differential mortality in carcinogenicity bioassays
options.C: Tumor incidence not adjusted for mortality

explanation: The polyk adjustment accounts for differential mortality in carcinogenicity bioassays. Adjusts tumor incidence for animals that died early

question_text: All of the following are correct regarding carcinogenicity EXCEPT:

options.B: Tumor incidence not adjusted for mortality
options.C: Historical controls not used
options.D: Peto analysis is the preferred statistical method for evaluating tumor incidence

explanation: Peto analysis is the preferred statistical method for evaluating tumor incidence. Accounts for competing risks of non-tumor death

question_text: All of the following are correct regarding genetic tox EXCEPT:

options.B: The Ames test uses Salmonella typhimurium strains to detect bacterial reverse mutations
options.C: Micronucleus detects only clastogenic effects

explanation: The Ames test uses Salmonella typhimurium strains to detect bacterial reverse mutations. Strains TA98, TA100 detect different mutation types; S9 provides metabolic activation

question_text: All of the following are correct regarding genetic tox EXCEPT:

options.B: In vivo micronucleus test detects clastogenic and aneugenic effects in bone marrow or blood
options.C: Ames test uses mammalian cells

explanation: In vivo micronucleus test detects clastogenic and aneugenic effects in bone marrow or blood. OECD TG 474; micronuclei contain chromosome fragments or whole chromosomes

question_text: All of the following are correct regarding genetic tox EXCEPT:

options.B: The comet assay (single-cell gel electrophoresis) detects DNA strand breaks
options.C: In vitro sufficient for assessment

explanation: The comet assay (single-cell gel electrophoresis) detects DNA strand breaks. Measures tail length and tail moment as indicators of DNA damage

question_text: All of the following are correct regarding genetic tox EXCEPT:

options.C: ICH M3 requires genotoxicity testing battery: Ames, in vitro chromosomal aberration, in vivo micronucleus

explanation: ICH M3 requires genotoxicity testing battery: Ames, in vitro chromosomal aberration, in vivo micronucleus. Must be completed before first human dosing

question_text: All of the following are correct regarding epigenetic EXCEPT:

options.C: DNA methylation at CpG islands typically silences gene expression

explanation: DNA methylation at CpG islands typically silences gene expression. Global hypomethylation and gene-specific hypermethylation are common in cancer

question_text: Which quantitative relationship correctly describes epigenetic?

options.C: No role in disease
options.D: Histone acetylation is generally associated with active gene transcription

explanation: Histone acetylation is generally associated with active gene transcription. HDACs remove acetyl groups, leading to gene silencing

question_text: Which quantitative relationship correctly describes guidelines?

options.A: GLP not required for safety studies
options.B: S1A requires studies for all drugs
options.C: OECD guidelines optional
options.D: ICH S1A requires carcinogenicity studies when drug is used clinically for 6 months or longer

explanation: ICH S1A requires carcinogenicity studies when drug is used clinically for 6 months or longer. Also required when carcinogenicity concern exists from SAR or short-term studies

question_text: Which quantitative relationship correctly describes guidelines?

options.C: ICH S1B allows alternative models (transgenic or 6-month) instead of two 2-year bioassays
options.D: GLP not required for safety studies

explanation: ICH S1B allows alternative models (transgenic or 6-month) instead of two 2-year bioassays. Reduces animal use while maintaining detection capability

question_text: Which quantitative relationship correctly describes guidelines?

options.A: GLP not required for safety studies
options.B: S1A requires studies for all drugs
options.C: OECD TG 471 describes the bacterial reverse mutation test (Ames test)

explanation: OECD TG 471 describes the bacterial reverse mutation test (Ames test). Uses Salmonella and/or E. coli with and without metabolic activation

question_text: Which quantitative relationship correctly describes guidelines?

options.B: OECD TG 474 describes the mammalian erythrocyte micronucleus test
options.C: S1A requires studies for all drugs

explanation: OECD TG 474 describes the mammalian erythrocyte micronucleus test. Bone marrow or peripheral blood in mice or rats

question_text: Which quantitative relationship correctly describes guidelines?

options.A: GLP regulations require nonclinical studies to be conducted per predetermined protocols with QA oversight
options.C: S1A requires studies for all drugs

explanation: GLP regulations require nonclinical studies to be conducted per predetermined protocols with QA oversight. Key elements: QA unit, SOPs, study director, raw data archival

question_text: Which quantitative relationship correctly describes guidelines?

options.A: S1A requires studies for all drugs
options.B: OECD GLP requires a Quality Assurance Program separate from the study director
options.C: OECD guidelines optional
options.D: GLP not required for safety studies

explanation: OECD GLP requires a Quality Assurance Program separate from the study director. QA performs inspections and audits to ensure data integrity

question_text: A toxicologist evaluating guidelines should consider which of the following?

options.A: S1A requires studies for all drugs
options.B: ICH Q3A requires identification of impurities above the identification threshold in drug substances
options.C: GLP not required for safety studies

explanation: ICH Q3A requires identification of impurities above the identification threshold in drug substances. Threshold depends on maximum daily dose

question_text: A toxicologist evaluating guidelines should consider which of the following?

options.A: ICH S7B requires hERG channel assay and telemetry study for QT prolongation assessment
options.C: GLP not required for safety studies
options.D: S1A requires studies for all drugs

explanation: ICH S7B requires hERG channel assay and telemetry study for QT prolongation assessment. In vitro hERG + in vivo conscious animal telemetry

question_text: A toxicologist evaluating guidelines should consider which of the following?

options.C: ICH S10 requires photosafety evaluation when drug has significant skin absorption
options.D: S1A requires studies for all drugs

explanation: ICH S10 requires photosafety evaluation when drug has significant skin absorption. Includes in vitro phototoxicity and in vivo photosafety assessment

question_text: A toxicologist evaluating epa regulations should consider which of the following?

options.B: EPA GLP (40 CFR 160) applies to FIFRA testing; 40 CFR 792 applies to TSCA testing
options.C: EPA does not require risk assessment

explanation: EPA GLP (40 CFR 160) applies to FIFRA testing; 40 CFR 792 applies to TSCA testing. Similar to 21 CFR 58 but specific to EPA-regulated testing

question_text: A toxicologist evaluating epa regulations should consider which of the following?

options.B: EPA does not require risk assessment
options.C: The Red Book describes EPA's four-step risk assessment paradigm

explanation: The Red Book describes EPA's four-step risk assessment paradigm. Hazard ID, dose-response, exposure assessment, risk characterization

question_text: A toxicologist evaluating dose response should consider which of the following?

options.C: NOAEL is the highest dose with no statistically significant adverse effect increase

explanation: NOAEL is the highest dose with no statistically significant adverse effect increase. LOAEL is the lowest dose with significant effect

question_text: A toxicologist evaluating dose response should consider which of the following?

options.A: Benchmark dose (BMD) uses the full dose-response dataset rather than relying on a single NOAEL
options.C: MOE used for threshold effects

explanation: Benchmark dose (BMD) uses the full dose-response dataset rather than relying on a single NOAEL. BMD10 = dose for 10% response above background
